articleTitle: Space segment for VSATS in Europe
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: Discusses the development of the 'SMS Open User Network' where the satellite transmission parameters and earth station characteristics are specified. The system is open to any user with an earth station conforming to the standards. The single channel per carrier (SCPC) frequency division multiple access (FDMA) technique used in the Open Network incorporates the necessary flexibility for sharing the SMS transponders between many different users. In addition to the Open Network, customer-tailored 'SMS Closed User Networks', for which transmission parameters and earth station characteristics would be defined by the users in line with their own requirements are also allowed to use the space segment. In closed networks, virtually any modulation or accessing technique can be accommodated, as well as a wide range of user bit rates, link qualities and earth segment configurations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of the D-MAC data channel as a carrier for business data services
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: One area of great interest is in the potential use of D-MAC DBS TV systems to support data services for business users. Any discussion of the use of D-MAC to provide data services must begin by placing the hypothetical D-MAC network (using the D-MAC data channel) in the context of the well-known ISO/OSI reference model. The generalised communications model for a D-MAC network is shown. A central host system interacts with a hub. The hub transmits data via a D-MAC carrier to a large number of receivers. Each receiver then interacts with a terminal to deliver information. Note that while the hub to receiver link is a one way broadcast link, the interfaces between the hub and host and the receiver and terminal are not similarly restricted. It is the first three layers-the physical, link and network layers-that are the subject of the paper. A model of these layers has been developed which allows detailed examination of the performance of a D-MAC network carrying a fully-compliant ISO protocol at the network layer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: With increasingly powerful satellites now becoming available or planned, the possibility of direct VSAT to VSAT communications without a hub becomes technically feasible. The administrative functions of the traditional star network hub station can now be assigned to one (or more) designated VSAT terminal, whilst permitting direct VSAT to VSAT communications in a mesh architecture. The paper describes two proposed experimental applications for VSAT mesh networks; firstly an E-mail system operating over a single 64 kb/s satellite channel, with a specially developed satellite access protocol which adapts to traffic load; secondly a video conferencing system operating at a user rate of 384 kb/s with TDMA access to the satellite. Both experimental applications are designed to operate over the Olympus Specialised Services Payload.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: The Contel ASC-DMN3000 system has been developed from the Starcom system, designed by engineers at Comsat Technology Products. A number of new software features have been included and the antenna and indoor unit have been redesigned. The system now incorporates various transmission modes based on time division multiple access. The Starcom product capability of TDM on the outbound and RA-TDMA on the inbound carriers, has now been enhanced to include fixed frame TDMA, reservation TDMA and random access with notification TDMA (RAN).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An overview of CODE: the CODE VSAT network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: The cooperative Olympus Data Experiment (CODE) is an experimental VSAT network which forms part of the Olympus Utilisation Programme. The central facilities and basic infrastructure are being organised by the European Space Agency. The VSAT terminals will be provided by various user organisations to their own designs. The overall design of the system is being established by an international team of engineers drawn from universities and technical establishments. The use of the 30/20 GHz for VSAT networks is of particular interest since although it permits the use of small stations, the network, nevertheless, has to cope with severe fading. The paper describes the system design and the application aspects of the experiment. The applicable hardware is also described in outline.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VSAT-an alternative communication network for fixed and mobile applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: The new generation of VSAT networks now offer personalised communication facilities from VSAT to hub or VSAT to VSAT which have hither been reserved for much larger earth stations. The new VSAT is therefore a viable competitor, for an alternative network, in parts of the world where a reliable line infrastructure does not exist, or for small private business networks or mobile/defence networks. By the more efficient use of bandwidth new technology has reduced the hub and satellite costs. Small VSAT networks are now commercially viable whilst retaining the expansion facilities to that of large networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The regulatory reality and its impact on satellite services in Europe
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: The main issues dealt with are as follows: equipment/terminal ownership and operation; the right to receive satellite transmissions; the right to transmit signals; and the ability to obtain a licence to offer services by satellite. West Germany, Sweden and the UK are the most liberal countries in Europe. Since the reorganisation of the Deutsche Bundespost which took effect from 1 July, 1989, there can be no doubt that, at least in theory, the most liberal of these is West Germany.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: Presents a new concept of using a broadcast data system to enhance a value added and data service (VADS) business. A satellite data broadcasting system is selected as the delivery mechanism but the principle applies equally well with terrestrial systems such as those which use the capacity provided by the blank lines of a broadcast television channel or the capacity provided by a subcarrier transmitted with a sound radio channel. The authors start by examining the nature of VADS, firstly from a regulatory viewpoint, then an information technology perspective and subsequently from a data communications standpoint. They then look at satellite data broadcast systems, also known as one way VSATs (very small aperture terminals), and considers how these can be integrated with VADS networks. The combination of VADS and VSATs is examined from an information technology viewpoint to see whether the combination offers more than the two parts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: DCC Limited, as part of the Hughes Aircraft Company, is closely linked with one of the major US suppliers of VSAT systems, Hughes network Systems (HNS). An important contribution to their success is the matching of technological developments to customer needs. Consideration of these developments in the context of market opportunities shows what is likely to sell-hence 'the user driven system'. HNS have developed the concept of the Integrated Satellite Business Network (ISBN). Nearly all applications involve a central location communicating with a large number of remote terminals, where the users of the remote terminals need to access information on a central database and the company's management needs to interrogate the remote sites to extract data. This requirement dictates the most common topology encountered in VSAT systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CODE Ka-band VSAT: hardware configuration and measurements, link and protocol simulation results
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on VSATs - Trends and Technologies
abstract: A number of CODE related activities are currently in progress at the University of Surrey. The activities can be classified in three categories. The co-ordination of the design, manufacture, and testing of a UK sourced CODE VSAT terminal, link performance simulation using TOPSIM and BOSS, and the simulation of candidate link protocols using the SIMSCRIPT simulation package. The final acceptance testing of the CODE terminal has taken place, and included transmission tests over the Olympus satellite. The link performance simulations have served as an input to the CODE design group. The protocol simulations represent an independent study of protocols that may be applicable to a VSAT system such as CODE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
